title: Impact of Writ of Election on Validity of Appointment as Grassroot Adviser
what_it_is: Impact of Writ of Election on Validity of Appointment as Grassroot Adviser

sections.label: GRA appointment term and duties
sections.summary: A GRA's term is set by PA, not tied to Parliament, and GRAs keep working and considering appeals after a Writ of Election.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The term of a GRA's appointment is determined by PA and is not tied to the term of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As with all Government agencies, which continue to function after a Writ of Election is issued, GRAs continue to discharge their responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In this period of time, Government agencies also continue to receive and will duly consider appeals made by members of the public, or those made on their behalf.

sections.label: Appeals by non-Members of Parliament
sections.summary: Such persons are not Members of Parliament, so any appeal they file is treated as a request made on behalf of another member of public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, to that extent, they are not Members of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Therefore, the appeal, if any is filed by that person, it will be treated as a request made on behalf of another member of public.
